summary: iia magnitudes in layer B are not on a common scale, so the magnitude_continuity check of assertion verification is UNUSABLE for iia assertions (27 of the 158 assertions the legacy bare-label tier was hiding, including the tier's largest, serbia|iia|1920-1944 at 573 rows). Measured on consolidated_layer_b.parquet (26,175 iia rows, 164 labels, 1909-1945), median wheat production in 'tonnes': canada 756,867; denmark 690,589; sweden 497,275; germany 293,228; france 101,145; united kingdom 96,525; serbia 14,618; netherlands 1,103. Denmark and Sweden are plausible for the interwar period; France (~8 Mt), Germany (~4-5 Mt), Canada (~10-14 Mt) and the Netherlands (~150 kt) are one to two orders of magnitude low, so the error is per-table, not a single global factor that could be divided out. Area is affected too: median wheat area in 'ha' 1930-1938 is russian federation 125,800, serbia 58,000, czech republic 5,000 - the USSR/Serbia ratio is 2.2 where the real one is ~90. Within one series the scale also flips: serbia wheat area is 58,000 ha for 1934 and 17,000 ha for the 1934-1938 average. Audit required: trace the unit column and any multiplier applied per iia publication/table during layer_b consolidation. Until then, iia assertions must be verified on scope/vintage/documentary grounds only and a verifier must not read iia staple_magnitudes as evidence of reporting scope. No polity or territorial action follows from this row. AUDIT DISCHARGED 2026-08-20, AND EVERY LEG OF THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS REFUTED. The entry asked to 'trace the unit column and any multiplier applied per iia publication/table during layer_b consolidation'. Done: of all 12,052 layer-B iia `tonnes` rows, 10,810 (89.7%) carry a value that appears VERBATIM among the raw extract's production values for the same year, and only 112 (0.9%) need a power-of-ten factor to find a raw match -- x10 29, x100 49, x1000 34, which is the size of the already-confirmed iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes / iia-hops-x100 / iia-1933-x10-wrong-volume-cells classes rather than a new one. A per-table rescaling during consolidation would produce a LOW verbatim rate; 90% is incompatible with it. THE MAGNITUDE EVIDENCE WAS A WRONG-ITEM COMPARISON. Both legs cited `wheat`, and iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin (confirmed, logged later) establishes that the iia `wheat` item is spelt and meslin -- the raw extract carries ZERO wheat production rows. Against raw spelt+meslin the layer-B medians are the SAME series, not one to two orders low: canada 756,867 vs 771,015; denmark 690,589 vs 745,022; sweden 497,275 vs 502,537; france 101,145 vs 97,650; uk 96,525 vs 87,906 (uk: england and wales). Those are plausible magnitudes for the crop they actually are -- Danish and Swedish blandsaed, French meteil, Canadian mixed grain -- and the Netherlands' 1,103 t, flagged here as absurd for wheat, is unremarkable for a minor mixed grain. THE AREA RATIO IS CORRECT IN LAYER B. This entry reads the USSR/Serbia area ratio as 2.2 'where the real one is ~90'; ~90 is a WHEAT ratio. For spelt+meslin the comparable raw quantity is the per-year SUM of the two products, and its medians give ussr 157,150 ha against yugoslavia 79,000 ha, a ratio of 1.99 -- so layer-B's 2.2 is right. (A first pass at this refutation reported 4.44 by taking the median of individual product ROWS instead of per-year sums, which is the same wrong-aggregate mistake in miniature.) CONSEQUENCE: the blocker on iia magnitude verification is ITEM IDENTITY, not scale, and it is documented by iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin and iia-item-series-switch-raw-products. The instruction above -- that iia assertions be verified on scope/vintage/documentary grounds only -- rests on refuted grounds and costs the 27 assertions this entry names, including its largest, serbia|iia|1920-1944 at 573 rows. STATUS LEFT AT pending_audit DELIBERATELY: refuting the evidence offered is not the same as proving iia magnitudes ARE on a common scale, which should rest on a positive test, and lifting a verifier instruction is a curation call.

label: (nested reporting levels; see summary)
summary: A polity can receive TWO OR MORE NESTING LEVELS of the same territory from the SAME source, so any aggregation over polity_code either sums a whole with its own parts or reads a cell that holds two incompatible values. Measured 2026-08-17 by routing all 189,839 matched layer-B rows through the assertion segments and grouping on (polity_code, source, item, indicator, year, unit): 52 such cells hold 110 rows contributed by more than one source label, and NONE of the colliding values are equal, so this is not duplicate ingestion but genuinely different series landing on one key. Worst cases: PNG-1949-1975 [fao1952] 18 rows from 'papua' + 'new guinea' (the two component territories FAO still reported separately after the 1949 union); CHN-1949-1950 13 rows and CHN-1947-1949 12 rows from 'china' + 'china 22 provinces' + 'china manchuria' (the 22-provinces rows are China proper EXCLUDING Manchuria: their land-use totals are 507,182 vs 106,930 thousand ha, i.e. ~5.07M km2 vs ~1.07M km2, so the two are disjoint components of the polity); FID-1887-1954 10 rows from 'indochina' + 'indochina viet nam'; KOR-1948-2025 10 rows from 'korea' + 'korea south'; DEU-1920-1938 9 rows from 'germany' + 'germany western' + 'germany berlin' for 1937 alone, which leaves the Reich polity carrying three mutually incompatible 1937 population values (Berlin's 4,284 thousand among them, against a Reich total near 67 million); JPN-1895-1945 [iia] 8 rows from 'japan' + 'palau'; GBR-1921-2025 8 rows from 'united kingdom' + 'united kingdom great britain' (Great Britain excludes Northern Ireland); CHN-1950-2025 6 rows; SER-1878-1913 [juan] 4 rows from 'serbia' + 'yugoslav sfr'; and 2 rows each on ETH-1907-1936/ETH-1936-1941/ETH-1941-1952 ('ethiopia' + 'ethiopia pdr'), PAL-1920-1948 ('israel' + 'palestine'), VGB-1800-2025 and ZAF-1910-2025 ('south africa' + 'natal'). Aggregate-level nesting without cell conflicts exists too and is not counted here (BWI-1833-1962 and BLI-1833-1960 beside their constituent islands; GCT-1919-1956 beside GHA-1898-1957 and BTL-1920-1957; PYF-1800-2025 beside 'makatea'; USA-1867-1959 beside 'alaska'/'guam'/'american samoa'/'virgin islands us'). This is the same hazard already recorded for one label in united-states-california-double-count, generalised and quantified. Audit required: decide, per family, which nesting level the polity represents, then either drop the other level (as the California row does) or give the component its own polity/segment. Fourteen legacy-tier assertions were quarantined rather than confirmed on this ground (see quarantine.csv, 2026-08-17); each names the missing segment where one exists: MAN-1945-1950 already covers 1945-1949 Manchuria, TNGU-1920-1949 and TPAP-1906-1949 end at the 1949 PNG union, BRL-1938-1945 and WZO-1938-1949 both start in 1938 so the 1937 Berlin and western-zone rows have no target, and the Caroline Islands have no polity for the 1914-1920 Japanese occupation (GCAR-1899-1914 -> CAR-1920-1945). No polity or polygon change is made here. WHAT THE AUDIT ACTUALLY REQUIRES, MEASURED 2026-08-20: for each family, does a polity exist whose TERRITORY is the component and whose span covers the conflicting years? Only ONE of ten does. CHN-1947-1949 and CHN-1949-1950 can send their `china manchuria` rows to MAN-1945-1950 (1947-1949 covered); CHN-1950-2025's 1950-1951 manchuria rows cannot, because that row ends exactly at 1950. Every other family needs a polity that does not exist: PNG-1949-1975's papua+new guinea rows are 1950-1951 while TPAP-1906-1949 and TNGU-1920-1949 both end at the union; DEU-1920-1938's berlin and western-zone rows are 1937 while BRL, WZO and SBZ all start in 1938; JPN-1895-1945's palau rows are 1915-1918, in the gap between GCAR-1899-1914 and CAR-1920-1945; KOR-1948-2025 receives `korea` meaning the PENINSULA for 1949-1951, for which no polity exists after KOR-1945-1948 (and the peninsula is NOT PRK); ZAF-1910-2025 receives `natal` after NAT-1895-1910 ends; GBR-1921-2025 receives Great Britain exclusive of Northern Ireland, which has no row; SER-1878-1913 receives `yugoslav sfr` decades before any Yugoslav polity. So the audit is not ten independent judgements -- for eight families the judgement is already implied by this entry's own framing and what is missing is the ROW, which makes those eight instances of issue 400 rather than of this audit. IT IS ALSO THE BOTTLENECK FOR THE QUARANTINE: 13 of the 34 quarantine rows with no review verdict scope-match this entry (china manchuria x3, china 22 provinces x3, germany berlin, germany western, palau, yugoslav sfr, united kingdom great britain, new guinea, papua), so a reviewer asked to adjudicate one of them is being asked this audit's question one cell at a time. Resolving this entry is therefore higher-leverage than working that queue. METHOD WARNING: a span-only test gives the wrong answer. Asking merely whether some polity sharing a code prefix covers the years returns 5 of 10, because PRK-1948-2025 covers 1949-1951 (but North Korea is not the peninsula), GBM-1895-1946 covers 1937 (but GBM is British MALAYA), and SER-1816-1913 covers 1909-1911 (but it is the same family, not a Yugoslav row). The territory has to be read, not inferred from the code.

label: (16 labels; see summary)
summary: 40 of the 607 iia tobacco rows (tonnes) are implausibly large: above 500,000 t for a single country when WORLD tobacco production in this period was on the order of 2-3 Mt. China mainland 1940 reads 51,345,800 t and the Russian Federation 1936 reads 27,600,000 t, each an order of magnitude above the world total. 16 countries, all years 1934-1945: algeria, chile, china mainland, czech republic, indonesia, iran, japan, myanmar, philippines, russian federation, serbia, south korea, syrian arab republic, thailand, turkey, zimbabwe. The other 567 rows look fine -- median 5,200 t -- so this is NOT a blanket rescaling of iia tobacco. FACTOR: where the same country has an ADJACENT-YEAR value from another source, the ratio is about x100 and is tight: nine countries splice mitchell->iia at 1939->1940 with a median ratio of 101, and back DOWN by the same factor at the 1940->1941 return seam (japan 86,000 t in 1939, 8,705,400 in 1940, 84,000 in 1941). Do NOT read the per-row ratios against DISTANT comparison years as factor estimates -- serbia's apparent x469 to x1610 compares 1934-1945 iia against a 1910 juan value, a 25-year gap, and says nothing about the multiplier. The precise factor per row is not established; the implausibility is. This is a specific instance of iia-layerb-magnitude-scale-inconsistent, and the seam evidence is recorded in state/source_splices.csv and guarded by scripts/validate_source_splices.py. Consumers should treat these 40 cells as unusable rather than scaling them, since the factor is inferred from neighbours rather than known. FACTOR NOW ESTABLISHED (2026-08-18, superseding this entry's earlier caution). The entry previously said the per-row multiplier was NOT established and told consumers to drop these cells rather than rescale them, because no (country, year) overlap existed to measure a factor against. A polity-level cross-source comparison supplies one: different labels routing to the SAME polity make independent sources directly comparable (786 such cells exist; see issue #375). Measured there, iia is EXACTLY 100x another source -- within 0.5% -- on 22 tobacco cells: 18 against `juan` across F248-1920-1947, F51-1918-1938, F51-1938-1945 and F51-1945-1947 (1934-1945), and 4 against `mitchell` on KOR-1800-1945 (1935-1941). TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, FIVE POLITIES, SAME FACTOR, and the 1934-1945 window is exactly the one this entry already recorded. Examples: F248 1934 iia 604,900 vs juan 6,049; 1937 iia 2,078,300 vs juan 20,783; KOR 1934 iia 1,540,400 vs mitchell 15,000. So for a cell with a cross-source comparison the repair is division by 100. For the remaining cells in the affected set there is no comparison and the factor is INFERRED, not measured -- treat those as unusable rather than rescaling them blind. Note what has NOT changed: the earlier retraction of ranking rows by ratio-to-NEAREST-source stands, since that method produced serbia at 'x1610' by comparing 1934-1945 iia against a 1910 juan value. The factor is established by same-year comparison at the same polity, which is a different and sound measurement. THE FACTOR IS NOW MEASURED WITHIN THE SOURCE, NOT INFERRED (2026-08-20), which supersedes this entry's caution that it is 'inferred rather than measured' wherever no cross-source comparison exists. 1933 is covered by BOTH a clean volume (iia_1933_34) and an inflated one (iia_1938_39), so the same label, product and YEAR can be read twice from the same publisher. Over 92 (label, product) pairs comparable within one year across that boundary -- 80 of them at the SAME year, where real growth is negligible -- the factor is: median exactly 100.0x, quartiles 99.8 / 100.0 / 100.0, and 81 of 92 within 20% of 100x, with NONE above 300x. Examples: mexico tobacco 1933 reads 9,524.2 t clean and 975,300 late (102.4x); french indochine 13,450 -> 1,401,000 (104.2x); turkey 35,367.1 -> 4,014,800 (113.5x). The publisher's own world-total row corroborates it independently: `total` / tobacco implied yield has a median of 0.929 t/ha for <=1933 and 92.232 for >=1934, a ratio of 99.3x, and an aggregate row cannot be produced by a per-cell transcription slip -- the table changed unit. CAUTION ON MEASURING IT ANY OTHER WAY: comparing a late-volume median against a clean-volume median WITHOUT matching the year gives a median of 111.6x with an interquartile range of 87.9-147.6 and outliers to 287x, because real growth in the 1930s is folded in -- british southern rhodesia's tobacco boom reads 242x. Likewise era_shift_verdicts.csv's ratio_to_own is a sound CONVICTION signal and a bad FACTOR estimate: british mauritius shows 2,254x because its baseline is its 1909 figure of 17.7 t, while the same label measured same-year is 91x (1932 clean 514 t against 1933 late 46,900). THREE PAIRS SIT AT 3-30x and are not explained by x100, matching the two cells this file already notes at 13.3x and 98.5x.

label: (4 polities; see summary)
summary: iia `hops` (tonnes) is carried 100x too large over 1934-1945, on the same evidence and in the same window as iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes -- and this commodity was NOT previously recorded. Measured by polity-level cross-source comparison (issue #375): iia is EXACTLY 100x `juan` on 15 cells, within 0.5%, across F248-1920-1947, F51-1918-1938, F51-1938-1945 and F51-1945-1947. Examples: F248 1935 iia 189,100 vs juan 1,891; 1937 iia 213,200 vs juan 2,132; F51 1934 iia 707,400 vs juan 7,074. World hop production in this period was on the order of 100,000 t, so 189,100 t for Yugoslavia alone is impossible on its own terms. That tobacco and hops share one factor, one window and one set of polities suggests a single extraction or unit fault affecting a group of items rather than a per-commodity error, so OTHER iia items in 1934-1945 should be checked the same way wherever a cross-source comparison exists. Two further cells sit at 13.3x and 98.5x rather than exactly 100x and are NOT explained by this. Repair for a compared cell is division by 100; for hops cells with no cross-source comparison the factor is inferred rather than measured. HOPS ALSO CARRIES A SEPARATE x10 ON ITS AREA, MEASURED 2026-08-20, and this entry's remedy is incomplete without it. Same-year 1933 pairs where iia_1933_34 and iia_1938_39 both report: hops PRODUCTION n=15, median factor 100.00x, 15 of 15 within 20% of 100x; hops AREA n=16, median 10.04x, 14 of 16 within 20% of 10x. For contrast tobacco AREA is CLEAN -- n=46, median 1.00x, 32 of 46 within 5% of 1x -- and across EVERY item zero area pairs fall in the 30-300x band, so the x100 is production-only and the hops area x10 is a second, distinct defect. THE LATE VOLUME ALSO ROUNDS IT: every late hops-area value is a multiple of 1,000 (hungary 107 -> 1,000; france 1,708 -> 17,000; uk 6,837 -> 68,000; usa 12,262 -> 123,000) against precise clean values, so the unit is ten times smaller AND rounded to the nearest 1,000 of it, i.e. the nearest 100 ha. That explains the only two apparent outliers: austria (56 ha -> 1,000) and romania (2 ha -> 1,000) sit BELOW the rounding floor, so their factors of 17.9x and 500x are the floor rather than a third defect -- the same grid-resolution phenomenon gated by validate_grid_ambiguous_zeros.py. THIS RECONCILES THE YIELD FIGURES: issue 433 records tobacco breaking at 70x and hops at 21x on implied yield with no explanation. Yield is production over area, so tobacco inflates 100/1 and hops 100/10 = 10. The items differ on yield BECAUSE hops' area is inflated too, which also means a yield-based screen understates hops tenfold and is likely why yield_series_corrections.csv reaches so few hops series. EXPOSURE IN THE PANEL, STATED AS AN INFERENCE: 38-41 layer-B hops area rows fall at 1934+, i.e. in the window where the defect was measured at its 1933 boundary. That the x10 CONTINUES past 1933 is an inference rather than a measurement -- same volume, same column, no reason to change mid-run -- because after 1933 there is no clean volume to compare against. Two weaker arguments were tried and both fail: the panel's hops-area median rising from 271 to 4,000 ha is confounded by composition, since different countries report in each period; and the on-a-1000-grid share is NOT a defect signature at all -- 96% of ALL 3,393 iia area rows at 1934+ sit on that grid, across 27 items with a median jump of 91 percentage points, which is the reporting grid already recorded for these volumes (see the iia grid convention and issue 446). Hops is BELOW the field at 50% on-grid, so the grid says nothing in its favour either way. REMEDY: hops production /100 AND hops area /10, with values under about 100 ha unrecoverable because the source rounded them to its floor. Dividing hops production alone would leave its area ten times high and its yield ten times low, which is worse than leaving both because it would look repaired. See issue #416.

commodity: (multiple: sugar, p, n, grapes, wheat, cotton lint, raisins)
summary: A layer-B iia ITEM SERIES can be stitched from several DIFFERENT raw products, switching year to year, so its level shifts are product switches rather than changes in output. 28 series mix raw products whose levels differ by >=3x, each product supplying >=2 cells. The switches go BACK AND FORTH, which is what rules out growth as the explanation. CLEAREST CASE, australia / sugar raw centrifugal / tonnes, 33 cells: cane 131,961 t (1912) -> BEET 922 (1913, x0.01) -> beet through 1919 -> cane 165,616 (1920, x105) -> cane 297,700 (1921) -> BEET 2,829 (1922, x0.01) -> `sugar: cane, unrefined` 537,212 (1925, x175) -> cane through 1938 (783,200) -> BEET 6,400 (1939, x0.01) -> cane 611,300 (1944, x873). Australia's beet sugar industry was negligible, so 12 of the 33 cells are about 1/300 of the series they sit in. OTHERS: sweden p (superphosphate -> basic slag x0.08 -> superphosphate x28); japan n (calcium cyanamide with ammonium sulfate in 1919 x27 and 1933 x5); japan p x26; norway p x17; congo and niger cotton lint (cotton vs cotton: ginned, 8-11x); czech republic grapes (grapes: table vs vineyards: all vs grapes: wine vs vineyards: grapes+raisins -- five products in a 17-value series, 8 ha against 27,000 ha); australia/cyprus/japan/israel/turkey grapes; usa and australia raisins. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the source never changes, so 16_source_splices.py sees no seam; the values are plausible for the product they came from, so no magnitude screen fires; and the item name is constant, so nothing keyed on it notices. CONSEQUENCE: any trend, growth rate or level-shift reading of an affected series is measuring the yearbook's choice of table, not agriculture. This is the mechanism behind part of issue #360's level-shift confound. NOT REPAIRABLE by rescaling -- each cell needs re-attributing to its own item. See issue #378. USA SUGAR IS THE MOST SEVERE INSTANCE AND ALSO SWITCHES TERRITORIAL SCOPE, not just product. `united states of america / sugar raw centrifugal / tonnes`, 33 dated cells, has FOUR regimes and NONE of them is a national total, each verified by exact subset-sum against the raw extract: 1909-1921 `usa`/BEET ONLY (39-81% of that year's US sugar, all cane missing); 1922-1925 `usa: louisiana and florida`/cane unrefined (4-19%); 1930-1938 CANE ONLY summed over `usa` + `us puerto rico` + `usa: hawaii`, beet excluded (77-90%) -- 1930 = 166,643.5 + 710,473.7 + 896,854.0 = 1,773,971.2 and 1938 = 491,800 + 827,000 + 835,000 = 2,153,800; 1939-1945 `usa: louisiana and florida`/cane (10-21%). So the scope oscillates between one state pair, the mainland's beet crop, and a three-territory cane aggregate. `puerto rico` routes to `united states of america` (kind=shares_target) and the raw carries its sugar continuously from 314,599 t in 1909 to 985,000 t in 1941, but it is inside the published figure ONLY for 1930-1938 -- included in 9 years of 33 and absent in the other 24. NOT double-counted: there are zero layer-B sugar rows under any Puerto Rico label, so the hypothesis was tested and refuted. Issue #443's account of this series is retracted in its own comments: its '1938 carries both 2,153,800 and 361,500' was a `1934-1938` PERIOD row read as a dated year, so there is no same-year duplicate and no interleaving at a point, and its '1909-1921 national scale' is beet only. See issues #443, #490.

label: (12+ labels incl. argentina, australia, belgium, chile, egypt, japan)
summary: The layer-B iia item `flax fibre and tow` is MAJORITY LINSEED -- the seed, not the fibre -- even though a separate `linseed` item exists (377 rows). Flax gives two products from one plant and they are not interchangeable: linseed is an oilseed, flax fibre and tow is a textile fibre, and the quantities differ by orders of magnitude for the same country. Measured against the raw IIA extract with the raw label required to match the layer-B label: of 543 `flax fibre and tow` cells, 168 match raw `linseed` and 109 match raw `flax: fibre`; 58 match BOTH and are ambiguous. So 110 cells are unambiguously LINSEED against 51 unambiguously flax fibre -- the item carries more of the crop it is not named for. 19 OF THOSE CELLS ARE ALSO PRESENT UNDER THE LAYER-B `linseed` ITEM at the same label, year, value and unit, so one observation is counted twice and any oilseed or fibre aggregate summing both items double-counts them. Magnitude check that makes the direction obvious: argentina appears with 1,590,000 t (1933), 2,025,000 t (1934) and 2,059,000 ha (1935) under `flax fibre and tow`. Argentina was the world's largest LINSEED producer and grew essentially no flax fibre; world flax fibre output was on the order of 500,000 t in total, so these are linseed figures. Also affected: australia, belgium, bolivia, chile, egypt, japan, mexico, new zealand, sweden, turkey, uruguay. NOT REPAIRABLE BY RESCALING: each cell needs re-attributing to the correct item, and the 58 ambiguous cells cannot be attributed from the panel at all. HYPOTHESIS, NOT MEASURED: issue #360's worst source splice is `united states / flax fibre and tow / ha` at x1655 across a juan->mitchell boundary, and a linseed-vs-fibre switch would produce exactly that. I cannot test it, because the raw extract I have is IIA's and that splice is between two other sources. See issue #380.

label: France Germany; France Eastern; Western; Eastern
summary: PROVEN BY ARITHMETIC: in fao1952's hemp-fibre table the labels `France Germany`, `France Eastern` and `Western` are GERMANY, GERMANY EASTERN and GERMANY WESTERN. The yearbook page listed France, then Germany with indented Eastern/Western sub-rows, and the extraction carried the preceding country name forward onto the sub-rows -- inconsistently, since `Western` kept no prefix. The proof is internal and needs no source page: `France Eastern` + `Western` = `France Germany` EXACTLY on both indicators for 1934-1938 -- production 2.9 + 1.2 = 4.1 (1000 t) and area 4.0 + 2.0 = 6.0 (1000 ha) -- which is the parent/child identity, and the table contains NO bare `Germany` label at all while carrying `France` separately at 3.9. A France-plus-Germany aggregate would not equal the sum of two German zones, and France's own row would not also be present. AFFECTED: 6 rows (2 per label). Small, but it is the only instance of this defect anywhere in the panel that can be settled from the numbers alone, so it is the template for the rest. WHAT THIS IS NOT: fao1952 encodes hierarchy by CONCATENATING parent and child, and that is normal and correct. `Germany Western` (254 rows), `China Taiwan` (143), `Korea South` (131), `Indochina Viet Nam` (109), `British Borneo Sarawak` (44) and `Libya Tripolitania` (37) are real parent-child labels; 46 labels share the surface pattern and 1,512 of their 1,567 rows are correctly assigned. The defect is only where the prefix is NOT a parent of the remainder -- `France Germany`, `Australia Fiji`, `Leeward Islands Trinidad and Tobago`, `Union of South Africa Zanzibar & Pemba` -- which takes geographic knowledge to tell apart and cannot be detected from the label shape. About 55 rows in total. See issue #29. WIDENED 2026-08-20: the bare label `Eastern` belongs here too, and the identity now holds for 18 rows rather than 6, by the same sum-identity method. The entry proved `France Eastern` + `Western` = `France Germany` in the hemp-fibre table. The same structure appears in TWO further tables, where the parent `Germany` is present under its own name and the residual is a CONSTANT third term: agricultural population 1937 W 10,091 + E 3,037 = 13,128 against Germany 13,145, and 1951 W 8,096 + E 3,488 = 11,584 against 11,601 -- residual exactly 17 BOTH years; goats 1949 W 1,428 + E 1,398 = 2,826 against 2,831, 1950 3,089 against 3,094, 1951 2,957 against 2,962 -- residual exactly 5 ALL THREE years. A residual that is constant across years is a third term, not noise, and Berlin is the only German unit unaccounted for in either table; `Germany  Berlin` does appear in the population table with agricultural sub-rows (32 occupied, 17 female, 15 male for 1951). CZECHOSLOVAKIA IS EXCLUDED: its agricultural population is 4,621 (1937) and 3,396 (1951) and its goats 982, none of which is close. That mattered because the magnitudes invite it -- `Western`'s 10,091 falling to 8,096 looks like the Czech lands losing the Sudeten German population, and it is only wrong because `Western` carries the AGRICULTURAL indicator while the Czech comparison figure is TOTAL population. ROW ACCOUNTING: `Western` has 13 layer-B rows and `Eastern` 5, all 18 UNROUTED (whep_code null). Of them, 7 are now settled arithmetically (2 hemp 1934-38 by the original proof, 2 population and 3 goats by the residuals above); 6 more are hemp 1949-1951 under `Western` alone, where no parent or sibling exists in those years, so they rest on continuity within a table whose label identity is proven; and the remaining period rows cannot reach published output either way (issue 310). The sibling labels already route -- `germany western` 254 rows to F78-1949-1990/DEU-1920-1938/WZO-1938-1949 and `germany eastern` 109 rows to F77-1949-1990/SBZ-1938-1949 -- so unlike issues 422 and 483 a destination exists, and 14 of the 18 rows (the 1949-1951 ones) are a mechanical reroute rather than a decision. The 2 rows dated 1937 land in issue 411's open question about post-war zones measured on 1937 territory. No alias changed.

label: czech republic; serbia; canada; russian federation
commodity: rye; flax fibre and tow; rapeseed; eggs
summary: 13 INDIVIDUALLY ATTRIBUTABLE defective cells, and unlike almost everything else in this file they are REPAIRABLE, because the correct value is known. Method: two labels that route to the same polity make two sources directly comparable; where they agree to within 1% on 70%+ of at least 8 shared years, they demonstrably measure the same thing, so a cell where they diverge by more than 2x is the defect rather than a difference of scope -- and the agreeing side supplies the value. A bare ratio cannot do this: it tells you two sources disagree, not which is wrong. iia `czech republic` vs juan `czechoslovakia`: rye (ha) 19/23 years agree, diverging 1939 (iia 98,000 vs juan 984,000), 1940 (78,000 vs 708,000), 1941 (78,000 vs 784,000), 1943 (26,000 vs 926,000); rye (tonnes) 18/23 agree, diverging 1942 (29,500 vs 1,231,000), 1943 (36,000 vs 1,536,000), 1944 (32,500 vs 1,214,000), 1945 (28,000 vs 981,000); flax fibre and tow (ha) 20/23 agree, diverging 1942 only (4,000 vs 43,000). iia `serbia` vs juan `yugoslav sfr`: rye (ha) 15/17 agree, diverging 1931 (24,415 vs 244,150) and 1932 (24,296 vs 242,961) -- both EXACTLY one tenth, 244,150/10 = 24,415 and 242,961/10 = 24,296.1; rye (tonnes) 17/18 agree, diverging 1945 where iia is the LARGER side (979,900 vs 92,000); rapeseed (tonnes) 15/16 agree, diverging 1920 (1,929 vs 3,900, x2.0). SHAPE: most divergences are near-exact powers of ten in one direction or the other, i.e. dropped or added digits in single cells, not a systematic rescaling -- the surrounding years match to the digit (czech rye 1930: iia 1,046,335 vs juan 1,046,335 exactly). The czech rye TONNES block 1942-1945 is the exception at x35-43 and is not a clean digit shift. NOT ESTABLISHED: which side is wrong in each case. The agreeing years prove the two measure one thing; they do not prove the majority is right. For czech rye the juan values are plausible for Czechoslovak rye (~700k-1M ha) and iia's 26,000-98,000 ha are not, so iia is the defective side there. serbia rye 1945 runs the other way and iia is the implausible one at 979,900 t. Each cell needs that check before it is repaired. CORRECTED 2026-08-18, SAME DAY: the 'dropped or added digits' reading above is WRONG for the czech cells, and so is the scope-flipping reading queued for the F51-1938-1945 wiki page. Inspecting the raw IIA extract directly, the `czechoslovakia` 1938-1945 block is internally corrupt: for RYE, either the area or the production value is implausible in 7 of the 8 years, and a yield check says which. 1938 reads 1,016,000 ha / 1,906,100 t = 1.88 t/ha, consistent. 1939 reads 98,000 ha / 1,729,400 t = 17.6 t/ha, so the AREA is the wrong cell. 1942 reads 861,000 ha / 29,500 t = 0.03 t/ha, so the PRODUCTION is the wrong cell; likewise 1944 (915,000 / 32,500) and 1945 (802,000 / 28,000). 1943 reads 26,000 ha / 36,000 t, internally consistent at 1.38 t/ha but both figures far too small for Czechoslovak rye. So the defective values are not digit-shifted versions of the truth -- they are numbers attached to the wrong (item, variable) slot in the extraction, which is why the two sides of the same year disagree with each other and not just with juan. The scope-flipping explanation is separately REFUTED: raw `german bohemia and moravia` exists but carries only butter, cheese and milk (21 rows, 1939-1945) and NO rye, so there is no sub-component rye series for the label to alternate with. Same block, same shape, other items: `tobacco` 1939 reads 6,000 ha with 933,000 t, and `hops` 1939 reads 10,500 ha with 763,400 t -- both the x100 defect already logged as iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes and iia-hops-x100. And the czech `flax fibre and tow` 1942 cell (4,000 vs juan's 43,000) is NOT a digit drop either: raw carries `flax: fibre` area 43,000 and `linseed` area 4,000 for 1942, so layer B took the LINSEED figure -- the conflation already logged as iia-flax-fibre-item-is-mostly-linseed. WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the serbia cells. 1931 (24,415 vs 244,150) and 1932 (24,296 vs 242,961) are still exact tenths, and no area/production misalignment is involved. The method also survives -- cross-source agreement on the surrounding years is what made these cells attributable at all -- but attributing them to a digit shift was reading a mechanism off a ratio. ADDED 2026-08-20, a 14th attributable cell and the first in this entry from a DIFFERENT source volume: iia `canada` / eggs, hen, in shell / tonnes / 1930 reads 148.7640 t where the correct value is almost certainly 148,764 t -- the same digits, shifted by 1000. The proof is internal to one volume: iia_1933_34 itself prints 146,658.666 for 1929, 153,376.3308 for 1931 and 148,415.3748 for 1932, so 148.764 sits three orders of magnitude below its own immediate neighbours in the same table, and 146,659 / 148.764 = 985.8. Canada produced roughly 150 kt of eggs a year through the interwar period; 149 TONNES is a village. THIS IS RAW-SIDE, not a consolidation error: the 148.7640 appears in the raw extract exactly as layer B carries it, so no multiplier was applied or lost downstream. ALREADY DETECTED: series_collapses.csv flags it as `interior_collapse` at factor 985.8 against the 1929 neighbour, so the screen was working -- what was missing is the repairable verdict, which this entry exists to hold. Unlike the czech rye cells corrected above, no (item, variable) misalignment is involved: the year, item and unit are all right and only the magnitude is wrong, which is why the digits recover the value. ADDED 2026-08-20, a 15th cell, and the only one in this entry whose correct value is DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE'S OWN ARITHMETIC rather than inferred from neighbours: iia `russian federation` / rye / tonnes / 1931 reads 21,990 t where it should read 21,990,000 t. iia_1933_34 prints two aggregate rows for the same year -- `total general including the ussr` 43,358,000 and `total general excluding the ussr` 21,368,000 -- whose DIFFERENCE is 21,990,000, i.e. the USSR's own rye production, exactly 1000x the printed cell. The neighbours agree independently: raw `ussr` rye is 23,600,000 (1930), 22,020,000 (1932) and 24,190,000 (1933), so 21,990,000 sits among them and 21,990 is three orders below. THE UNIT HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED: I first read this as thousand-tonnes beside tonnes within one series, because the convention at (iia, russian federation, *) establishes that label as whole-USSR scope and a mixed-unit series was the obvious explanation. The aggregate difference rules it out -- the source's own total is in tonnes and its residual is 21,990,000, so the cell is a decimal shift, not a unit. ALREADY DETECTED, like the canada cell above: series_collapses.csv carries it as `interior_collapse`, value 21990, neighbour 2.202e+07, factor 1001.4 -- and note the factor is 1001.4 rather than 1000 precisely because the neighbour is 1932's 22,020,000 rather than the true 1931 value, which is why a neighbour ratio cannot supply a repair and the aggregate difference can.

label: united states of america; canada; argentina
summary: RESOLVES issue #360's two largest recorded source seams, and NOT by the mechanism that issue proposed. `united states / flax fibre and tow / ha` jumps x1655 at a juan->mitchell boundary and Canada x1231; #360 offered a unit or thousands-multiplier mismatch as the leading candidate. Proof is exact equality with juan's own separately-labelled linseed series for the same country: united states 1950 mitchell flax-fibre 1,655,000 ha == juan linseed 1,655,000; 1952 mitchell 1,337,000 == juan 1,337,000; 1900 and 1901 likewise. canada 1952 mitchell 469,000 == juan linseed 469,000 (at 1951, the crop-year offset). Across the whole panel, 55 of the 204 mitchell `flax fibre and tow` (ha) values exactly equal a juan LINSEED (ha) value for the same country, against just 1 of 204 that equals a juan FLAX FIBRE AND TOW value -- a 55:1 ratio against the control, which rules out coincidence as the account of the bulk. Some of the 55 sit at a +/-1 year offset, which is the southern-hemisphere crop-year convention (argentina mitchell 1911 == juan 1912, and so on through 1922). THE YIELD IDENTITY CORROBORATES INDEPENDENTLY. juan's US flax-fibre series runs 3,000 ha and 1,900 t (1945) down to 1,000 ha and 400 t (1949), i.e. 0.30-0.63 t/ha, which is fibre flax. Mitchell's 1,655,000 ha against juan's 1950 fibre production of 100 t would imply 0.00006 t/ha. US linseed yields 0.46-0.70 t/ha across the same years, which is what these areas belong to. SCOPE: this is the same conflation already logged as iia-flax-fibre-item-is-mostly-linseed, now shown to affect MITCHELL as well as IIA -- so it is a property of how the item was harmonised rather than of one source. summary: CONFIRMED ORPHAN CELL: iia/czech republic/rye/ha reads 3.0 at 1910, while the series' next observation is 732,970 ha in 1919 -- a factor of 244,323, the largest leading_collapse in state/series_collapses.csv. Present in the raw extract as `czechoslovakia / rye / area / 1910 = 3.0 hectares` (iia_1909_21), so it is a source-side cell and not introduced downstream. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS TO REJECT IT, neither needing a magnitude argument. (1) Raw `czechoslovakia` carries exactly THREE rows dated before 1919, and the state was founded in October 1918: this 1910 rye area, a 1918 sugar-beet production of 640,816.1 t and a 1918 potato export of 0.1 t. The 1918 sugar beet is defensible -- the 1918 harvest reported under the successor state -- but a 1910 row predates the polity by eight years. (2) 3 ha is not a plausible rye area for any reporting unit that reports rye at all; the label's own body runs 732,970-899,842 ha. REMEDY: the cell should be missing. It routes to CZE-1804-1918 (Czech Lands), which is the right polity for 1910 -- the defect is the value and the row's existence, not the routing. A NEGATIVE RESULT FROM THE SAME SEARCH, recorded so it is not repeated: scanning all raw labels for an earliest year separated from the body by >=5 years with <=5 rows in the head returns FIVE candidates and only this one is a defect. `china` [1914], `china: manchuria` [1915-17], `french guiana` [1909-13] and `french west africa` [1918-19] all carry plausible values for territories that existed in those years -- so time-isolation is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and convicting a case needs the label's founding date, which is curation rather than measurement. Not gateable.

summary: 14 CONFIRMED cells where layer B took a 1933-era value ten times too small, and the correct figure is printed by another yearbook volume, so these are REPAIRABLE without a source consultation. Issue 424. THE TEST IS PROVENANCE-LINKED, not value-plus-year: matching a small round value against the raw extract by value and year alone left 9 of 16 uncertain, because 30, 300 and 2,100 appear all over the panel. The stronger condition adds a third requirement -- the layer-B label carrying the value must be the one state/item_provenance.csv attributes to that raw label. A coincidence has no reason to land on the provenance-linked label. Applying it: 14 confirmed, 2 coincidences discarded (the original 16 becomes 14). THE CELLS, as raw label / product / layer-B value / other volume's value / layer-B label: french dahomey/cacao: raw/30/300/benin; french dahomey/eggs 1932/129/1,294/benin; new zealand/hops/206/2,000/new zealand; french ivory coast/tobacco/334/3,300/ivory coast; british jamaica/cacao: raw/390/4,000/jamaica; french tonkin/tea/406/4,000/viet nam; french syria and lebanon/cottonseed/780/8,000/syrian arab republic; dutch east indies/sesame/1,580/16,000/indonesia; yugoslavia/hops/1,694/17,000/serbia; british antigua/sugar: cane/2,100/21,000/antigua and barbuda; czechoslovakia/hops/10,267/103,000/czech republic; peru/cottonseed/13,048/130,000/peru; japan/soybean/32,367/324,000/japan; australia/sugar: cane/65,129/636,200/australia. WHY NO DETECTOR CATCHES THEM: a x10 shift in a single cell clears no magnitude bound, opens no year gap and sits at a plausible number. The class is visible only by comparing volumes, which is what state/edition_conflicts.csv made possible -- 99 revisions differ by a clean power of ten and 98 hold the smaller value in iia_1933_34, against a 55% base rate across all 1,032 inter-volume revisions. label: (93 broken labels; largest is `[error] inde` with 340 cells)
commodity: (multiple: tobacco, coffee, cotton, rubber, tea, cottonseed, potatoes, fertilizers)
summary: 1,237 rows of the raw IIA extract carry a COUNTRY LABEL that begins with the literal string '[error]' -- 93 distinct broken labels, 0.43% of the 288,121-row extract, and every one of them still carries a value. 573 are production/area; the rest are trade (imports/exports/consumption/reexports 521) and other variables (143). The PRODUCT column is clean -- 0 rows have a broken product label -- so the corruption is specific to the country axis. By volume: iia_1938_39 429, iia_1939_45 259, iia_1925_26 204, iia_1933_34 179, iia_1909_21 128, iia_1929_30 38. EXPOSURE: fingerprinting each broken label's (year, value) set against all 164 layer-B iia labels, keeping only labels with >=6 distinct values, 517 cells clear the floor and 509 have NO layer-B label matching even half -- the best matches sit at 0-8%, which is what no match looks like. Only `[error] cameroun (mandat` at 25% suggests any of its data landed. THE LARGEST BLOCK IS NOT A DUPLICATE: `[error] inde` has 414 production/area rows, 340 with a usable year and 315 distinct values, best layer-B match 1.8%. The extract carries `british india` and four sub-labels properly, so the innocent reading was that this is the same data with a broken label; checked per cell on (product, year, unit, variable), 11 are identical to a british india cell, 15 DIFFER from it, and 388 have no british india cell at all. TWO MECHANISMS ARE MIXED, and only one is recoverable. (a) Mis-transcribed territory names where the intended label is legible: inde, sttisse (Suisse), sudde (Suede), tehecoslovaquie, russic (Russie), remaion (Reunion), togo (zone sous mandat, cameroun (mandat, syrie et liban (m, palestine (mand, territoires sous mandat japonais, trinite et tabago -- several appearing under three or four different corruptions of one name (togo (zone, togo (mandat, togo (maudat, togo (zoue), which is itself evidence of OCR rather than a source quirk. (b) Non-territory text absorbed into the country column, never recoverable as a territory because it never was one: culture des indigenes ('indigenous cultivation', a scope qualifier), culture associee, commerce avec le japon / hawai / porto-rico (trade-table column headers), par terre, continent, inland, exportations, y compris pu rss, and glued pairs like union de l'afrique du sudetats-unis and asiebirmanie -- which is why trade variables are over-represented. IDENTIFIED 2026-08-20, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE LABEL'S NAME: `[error] inde` IS BRITISH INDIA. The earlier entry said this could not be claimed because the cells match nothing; that was wrong -- 26 of the block's 414 production/area rows DO have a `british india` counterpart, and where both report the same product, year, unit and variable the values agree within edition-revision noise: guano natural 4,700 vs 4,710 (0.998), tea area 331,000 vs 330,000 (1.003), cottonseed 2,116,300 vs 2,101,060 (1.007), rapeseed production 613,700 vs 617,800 (0.993), groundnut production 3,237,100 vs 3,286,910 (0.985), tobacco area 471,000 vs 490,500 (0.960), groundnut area 3,070,000 vs 3,284,000 (0.935), sesame production 481,600 vs 543,600 (0.886) -- eight of nine within 7%. ALL the overlapping cells are at 1933, which is where they should be, since 1933 is the only year two volumes cover. Provenance corroborates: the block is entirely iia_1938_39 (245 rows) and iia_1939_45 (204), spanning 1933-1945, i.e. the late-volume India series with a broken country label. So 388 of its 414 rows are non-duplicating British India production/area cells. RECOVERY IS NOT CLEAN: its tobacco production reads 38.2-64.9 MILLION tonnes on 412,000-539,000 ha, i.e. 124 t/ha, which is impossible and becomes an ordinary 1.24 t/ha divided by 100 -- the x100 era defect of iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes and iia-hops-x100, so importing the block without that remedy imports 15 inflated cells. That also confirms the 1933 mechanism directly: the raw iia_1938_39 figure AT 1933 is inflated, and 1933 is clean in layer B only because iia_1933_34 supplies a second opinion the pipeline prefers. NOT A DEFECT OF THIS REPO: the corruption is upstream in the extract, so the open question is whether to record the loss (as #414 does for blank-as-zero) and whether the legible subset is worth recovering by hand; the togo/cameroun mandate rows are territories this database has a live interest in. Found while generalising #422's Karafuto test. See issue #493.

label: China
commodity: pigs; buffaloes; meat; wool clean basis; slaughter fats other than pig
summary: SIX CELLS UNDER fao1952's `China` LABEL CARRY IMPLAUSIBLY SMALL VALUES, while the label itself is a correct national total -- so this is per-cell damage, NOT a mislabelled or misrouted series. Issue #449 concluded from pigs and buffaloes that 'the China figure is not a national total ... the two labels are not the same territory'; that label-level conclusion is NOT supported. THE LABEL IS CHINA: use total 973,629 (1000 ha) = 9.74 million km2, China's land area; population total 452,460 (1937) and 463,500 (1951) thousand people; use land 944,420, built-on/wasteland 604,456, permanent pasture 194,133, arable 91,040; oats 730-792 kt on 940-959 kha; wool greasy basis 40/40/30 kt. The whole/parts relation is also right: use total reads China 973,629 against `China 22 provinces` 507,182, i.e. the parts are 52% of the whole, exactly what is expected when the 22 provinces exclude Manchuria, Tibet, Sinkiang and Mongolia. THE BROKEN CELLS: pigs 1949 = 95 against `China 22 provinces` 59,510 (China's 1949 herd was about 58 million head); buffaloes 1949 = 658 against 9,460 (about 9.5 million); buffaloes 1950 = 656 and 1951 = 568; meat 1950 = 1 and 1951 = 3 (1000 tonnes, for a nation); wool clean basis 1951 = 1 against 22 in both 1949 and 1950; slaughter fats other than pig 1948 = 30 against the 22 provinces' 1. NO SINGLE UNIT ERROR EXPLAINS THEM, which is the argument for per-cell treatment: pigs x1000 gives 95 million, above the 22 provinces' 59.5 million and plausible; but buffaloes x1000 gives 658 million against a WORLD buffalo population of roughly 45 million, x100 gives 65.8 million which is still above the world total, and x10 gives 6.58 million which is now BELOW the 22 provinces' 9.46 million. Every multiplier fails. NOT REPAIRABLE: the 22-provinces figure is a lower bound on the national one, not a substitute for it, so unlike iia-attributable-single-cell-errors no correct value is recoverable from within the panel. The consumer averages rather than sums duplicate keys, so a cell holding both the whole and a part publishes a blend; see layerb-nested-reporting-levels-one-polity for that population. See issue #449.

label: Malaya Federation of and Singapore
summary: ONE CELL, PROVEN BY ITS OWN SIBLING ROWS: `Malaya Federation of and Singapore` / population female agricultural occupation / 1937 reads 1,171 (1000 people), which is IDENTICAL to the same label's population agricultural TOTAL for 1937, also 1,171. A female agricultural population cannot be 100% of the agricultural population. The 1951 rows of the same label show what the correct structure looks like: agricultural total 1,186 = female 347 (29%) + male 839 (71%), summing exactly. The 1937 MALE row is absent entirely, so the signature is a COLUMN SHIFT at extraction -- the total's value landed in the female column and the male value was lost. NOT REPAIRABLE: the correct 1937 male/female split is not recoverable from the panel, because no other label carries a male/female agricultural breakdown for this territory and year. FOUND while testing issue #355's fourth whole-on-part case, which DISSOLVES: this issue read `Malaya Federation of and Singapore` (5 rows) as overstating against `Malaya Federation of` (76 rows), but all five rows are AGRICULTURAL-population rows while the larger label carries only population TOTAL plus crops, so the two never occupy the same cell and nothing is double-counted by summing the polity's rows. A hypothesis worth recording as refuted: 1,186 thousand is far too small for Malaya plus Singapore in 1951 (about 6.4 million together) and close to Singapore alone (1,045), which suggested a mislabel -- but the value is an AGRICULTURAL population, an ordinary 22% of Malaya's 5,337 total, so the magnitude argument alone would have produced a false reroute. See issue #355.

label: reunion (raw: french reunion); romania
summary: TEN FALSE EXONERATIONS IN era_shift_verdicts.csv, caused by a baseline drawn from the inflated volume. The era screen convicts a no-area row when it is >=30x the label's OWN pre-1934 median. For `reunion` that median is 20,000 t, which is itself an inflated figure, so every era row divides one inflated number by another and reads as consistent: ratio_to_own 1.00 for 1934/1935/1936 and 0.76-1.11 for 1939-1945, all filed no_area_level_consistent and none convicted. THE RAW SERIES SHOWS THE TRUTH: french reunion tobacco production reads 423.1 t (1926) and 348.4 t (1927) from iia_1929_30, then 20,000 t at 1933 and 1934-1936 from iia_1938_39, then 15,200-22,300 for 1939-1945 from iia_1939_45. A few hundred tonnes to 20,000 is a 47x step at 1933. Reunion is 2,512 km2, so a few hundred tonnes is the plausible figure and 20,000 is not. WHY THE 1933 SECOND OPINION DID NOT RESCUE IT: iia_1933_34 carries NO DATED 1933 production for this label -- only an undated 670.8 t row -- so there was nothing to outvote the late volume, the inflated figure filled 1933, and it became the baseline for every later year. THE CONDITION IS BROADER THAN THAT, established by a second case: `romania` / hops is contaminated too even though iia_1933_34 DOES supply a clean dated 1933 (9.5 t on 2 ha, beside 29.9 / 48.3 / 15.1 t for 1930-1932). Its recorded baseline is 1,770, which is exactly (3,500 + 40.6) / 2 -- the mean of the clean `1925-1929` period row from iia_1933_34 and the INFLATED `1928-1932` period row from iia_1938_39. Because the era baseline includes pre-era PERIOD rows, one inflated period row contaminates it regardless of how many clean dated years exist. So the general condition is that a pre-1934 baseline is clean only where EVERY pre-era row feeding it -- dated or period -- comes from a volume without the x100, not merely where a dated 1933 exists. That makes romania hops 1934-1938 an eleventh false exoneration on the same mechanism. NOT A THRESHOLD PROBLEM: the other ten no_area_level_consistent rows sit at 3.2x to 27.1x their own baseline and are simply under the 30x line (jordan 27.1, mauritania 25.0), which is a conservative-line question rather than a contaminated one. The 348 convictions are unaffected. See issue #416.
